subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Salpingectomy, Arias-Stella, Heterotopic and Scar Pregnancy

steps.tx: Removal of the affected fallopian tube with the ectopic pregnancy is **salpingectomy**. It is preferred when the tube is ruptured, badly damaged or the other tube is healthy. Future fertility remains good with one healthy tube. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Salpingectomy removes the affected tube and fertility stays good with one healthy tube.

steps.tx: Exaggerated glandular changes in the endometrium under ectopic hormonal influence form the **Arias-Stella reaction**. Pathologists see hyperchromatic, enlarged nuclei in endometrial glands. Its presence without villi supports ectopic pregnancy historically, though ultrasound now leads diagnosis. Correlating this finding with imaging and laboratory results prevents both delayed treatment and unnecessary intervention in most patients.
steps.say: The Arias-Stella reaction shows exaggerated endometrial glands under ectopic hormone influence.

steps.tx: Simultaneous intrauterine and extrauterine pregnancies together form **heterotopic pregnancy**. It is rare naturally but rises sharply with assisted conception. Seeing an intrauterine sac must never end the search for a second ectopic in these women. Early recognition matters because timely treatment gives clearly better outcomes than waiting for complications to develop first.
steps.say: Heterotopic pregnancy combines intrauterine and ectopic gestation, rising with assisted conception.

steps.tx: Implantation in the cervix below the internal os is **cervical ectopic** pregnancy. It bleeds torrentially if disturbed by curettage. Methotrexate, balloon tamponade and uterine artery embolisation preserve the uterus in stable cases. Students should connect this fact with the presenting symptoms, since examination questions usually test that clinical link directly.
steps.say: Cervical ectopic bleeds torrentially if disturbed and needs uterus preserving strategies.

steps.tx: Implantation into a previous caesarean scar defect is **caesarean scar pregnancy**. The thin scar risks rupture and morbidly adherent placenta if pregnancy continues. Early diagnosis allows methotrexate or surgical options before catastrophe. Documenting this finding clearly in the notes guides the next clinician and supports safe, well planned further management.
steps.say: Caesarean scar pregnancy implants in the scar defect and risks rupture if continuing.

steps.tx: Choosing tube removal over conservation depends on the other tube and future plans, a **fertility centred decision**. With a healthy contralateral tube, salpingectomy and salpingostomy give similar subsequent pregnancy rates. Conservation wins only when the other tube is compromised. When this picture is seen in practice, urgent senior review is wise whenever there is any doubt about severity.
steps.say: Fertility centred choice favours conservation only when the other tube is compromised.

steps.tx: Persistent trophoblast after conservative surgery is detected by plateauing hormone, termed **persistent ectopic**. About one in ten salpingostomies are affected. Methotrexate treats most without further surgery. Understanding this mechanism explains the symptoms, the investigation findings and the logic behind each step of treatment given.
steps.say: Persistent ectopic after salpingostomy shows plateauing hormone and responds to methotrexate.

steps.tx: Interstitial and cornual pregnancies may need wedge resection of the uterine cornu, an operation of **cornual resection**. Medical treatment succeeds in early stable cases increasingly. Late rupture of these remains among the deadliest ectopic events. This distinction changes management, so it should be settled early rather than after empirical treatment has already begun.
steps.say: Cornual resection treats interstitial pregnancies, whose late rupture is among the deadliest.

steps.tx: After any ectopic, future pregnancy planning includes early location scanning, termed **recurrence counselling**. Recurrence risk is about one in ten. Contraception until hormone resolution and folate optimisation complete the advice. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Recurrence counselling plans early location scanning in every future pregnancy.
